transcript.text:
Try these quick checks first:

1. Check power
• Make sure the oven is plugged in / cooker switch is on.
• Check the breaker or fuse box for a tripped circuit.
• If the display is blank, it may simply have lost power.

2. Check the clock/timer
• Many ovens will not heat after a power cut until the clock is set or the timer is set to manual mode.
• Look for a clock symbol, “AUTO,” or a hand/manual button.

3. Check the controls
• Select an oven function (bake/fan/grill), then set a temperature—not just one or the other.
• Some models need the function dial turned away from “off” before heating starts.

4. Door and child lock
• Ensure the door is fully closed.
• Check whether a child lock/control lock is active.

5. If it is a gas oven
• Make sure the gas supply valve is open.
• If you smell gas, do not try to light it or use electrical switches. Open windows, leave the area, and contact your gas emergency service or a qualified engineer.

6. If it turns on but does not heat
• A failed heating element, thermostat, igniter (gas), or control board may be the cause. This usually needs an appliance technician.

Tell me whether it’s electric or gas, and what happens when you try it—completely dead, display on but no heat, error code, clicking, etc.—and I can narrow it down.
its electric, Neff. display is flashing 0.00 and a little symbol, knobs do nothing. started after a power cut last night

That is very likely the clock needing to be reset after the power cut. On many Neff ovens, the oven controls are disabled while the display flashes 0:00 / a clock or automatic-cooking symbol.

Try this:

1. Find the button with a clock, timer, or menu symbol near the display.
2. Press it (sometimes repeatedly) until the clock/time symbol flashes.
3. Turn the control dial, or use the + / – buttons, to set the current time.
4. Press the clock button again, or wait a few seconds, to save it.
5. Make sure any “AUTO” / cooking-programme symbol has gone out. If it remains, press and hold the timer/clock button or use the button marked with a hand/manual symbol until it returns to manual operation.

Then try selecting an oven function and temperature again.

If the display stays frozen or the knobs still do nothing after setting the time, switch the oven circuit off at the cooker isolation switch or breaker for about 1 minute, turn it back on, and set the clock again.

Don’t remove panels or attempt internal repairs.
ok that worked, set the time and it came on and heated. thanks
Glad it’s working again. Power cuts often reset the Neff clock and put it into automatic mode, which prevents the oven from heating until the time is set.
